sources.entry: scapy - A brilliant packet manipulation library.

summary.one_liner: Scapy is a Python-based interactive packet manipulation program and library for forging, decoding, sending, capturing and storing network packets.
summary.what_it_does: Scapy can forge or decode packets across many protocols, send them onto the wire, capture them, and read or write pcap files. It can match requests to replies and is designed for fast packet prototyping using defaults that work. The README says it can handle tasks such as scanning, traceroute, probing, unit tests, attacks and network discovery, and lists tools it can replace, including hping, most of nmap, arpspoof, arping, tcpdump, wireshark and p0f. It also covers unusual tasks like sending invalid frames and injecting custom 802.11 frames. It is usable as an interactive shell or as a Python library.
use_cases: craft and send custom network packets
capture and analyze packets to pcap files
security testing and ARP spoofing experiments
how_to_run: sudo ./run_scapy (as shown in the shell demo for network access)
notable: Works with no external Python modules on Linux and BSD-like systems
Usable both as an interactive shell and as a library
Can replace many classic tools such as hping, nmap (partially), tcpdump and wireshark
Supports injecting invalid frames and custom 802.11 frames
caveats: On Windows, mandatory dependencies must be installed separately as described in the documentation
Optional features such as plotting need extra Python modules like matplotlib or cryptography
Some demo examples in the README may be outdated
